hypothesis: Replacing Opus 4.8 with Opus 5 changes model reliability and contribution to a mixed civilization while all other experimental controls remain fixed.

controls.control_completion: Both existing cells completed tick 40 and passed the startup health gate. Seed 41 recorded one isolated Sonnet decision failure; Opus 4.8 recorded no provider failures.
controls.code_equivalence: The control cells ran at 0a05b0f. From 0a05b0f through treatment launch commit cf99d93, changes are documentation-only; agent_world and tests are identical.
controls.treatment_scope: Only the explicit Claude model identifier for the six Opus agents changes from claude-opus-4-8 to claude-opus-5.
controls.quota_policy: Any incomplete provider-failure or quota-failure tick is discarded, preserved in a separate partial-usage ledger, and resumed only from the last completed-tick checkpoint.

primary_model_outcomes: trade offers, acceptances, gifts, and communication
analysis_policy.interpretation: Use paired-seed differences and require directional replication before attributing effects to Opus 5. Normalize failures by submitted actions or decisions and economic activity by successful calls or starting population as appropriate. Treat the unchanged cohorts as indicators of systemic spillovers and background stochastic variation.

completion.control_quality_note: Both controls passed their health gates. Seed 41 had one isolated Sonnet failure; neither Opus 4.8 control cohort had a provider failure.

replicated_directions: Opus 5 had a lower invalid-proposal rate, fewer action-point exhaustion errors, more survivors or equal survival, more communication, more trade participation, more gifts, and more owned assets in both seeds.
Opus 5 had higher contention, output tokens, and latency in both seeds.

The Opus 5 civilizations had fewer invalid proposals, fewer damage events, more fixed capital, more trade offers, greater accepted trade value, more gifts, more communication, less stored inventory, and worse upkeep completion in both seeds.
results.important_spillover: Sonnet survival fell from 10/12 in the Opus 4.8 controls to 4/12 in the Opus 5 worlds, with a decline in both seeds, even though Sonnet invalid-proposal rates improved. Overall survival therefore changed only from 49/60 to 50/60.
results.conclusion: Opus 5 is a substantially stronger raw planner and a much more active entrepreneur and coordinator than Opus 4.8 in this benchmark. It also consumes roughly twice the output tokens and is about 80 percent slower per call. The resulting civilizations form more capital and exchange more value but do not show a comparably large survival or aggregate-wealth gain, and the replicated Sonnet survival loss requires a dedicated follow-up before interpreting the ecosystem effect as uniformly beneficial.
